{"code": "import statsmodels.api as sm

# Since scipy is not available, use statsmodels for chi-squared test
# We'll use a simple contingency table and compute chi-squared manually
observed = pd.crosstab(df['sex'], df['arm'])

# Compute expected frequencies under independence
expected = np.outer(observed.sum(axis=1), observed.sum(axis=0)) / observed.sum()

# Compute chi-squared statistic
chi2 = ((observed - expected) ** 2 / expected).sum().sum()

# Degrees of freedom for 2x2 table is (2-1)*(2-1) = 1
dof = 1

# Compute p-value using chi2 distribution
p_value = 1 - sm.stats.chi2.cdf(chi2, dof)

print(f'Chi-squared statistic: {chi2:.4f}')
print(f'P-value: {p_value:.4f}')
print(f'Expected frequencies:\n{expected}')"}
